checks_performed: Read only the specified source JSON, specified draft JSON, and the checker created in the designated audit directory; did not use the web.

Reconstructed the exact-size semantics, greedy recurrence and repair, boundary cases n=0, q=0, q=1, and q=n, sparse isolation construction, edge-edit transfer, additive approximation, bounded-degree ratio, and Vertex Cover gadget.

Created and ran an exact-integer exhaustive checker. It passed on all simple graphs of orders 0 through 6 for Claims 0–5 and 9; all graph pairs of orders 0 through 4 for Claims 6–8; and 559 isolate-free maximum-degree-three graphs through order 5, including 362529 dominating-set conversions, for Claim 10.

The checker made every radius and residual decision by integer cross-multiplication. It reported 3316 constructive one-edge transfers, 82581 gap cases, and 137870 additive-transfer cases without failure.
Audited Claims 11–12 deductively. Claim 12 was checked only as a conditional implication; the external APX-hardness premise itself was not independently sourced.
Compared the exact unconditional all-c target against the draft's actual scope and its final headline.

claims.claim: For 0≤q≤n, a graph has a dominating set of exactly q vertices if and only if its domination number γ is at most q.
claims.evidence: An exact-q dominating set immediately gives γ≤q. Conversely, a minimum dominating set of size γ≤q can be enlarged with q−γ unused vertices because q≤n, and every superset of a dominating set remains dominating. This also covers the empty graph.
claims.search_method: Direct proof plus exhaustive enumeration of every simple graph on 0–6 vertices and every q.

claims.claim: Greedy closed-neighborhood coverage has residual r≤n(1-1/q)^q whenever γ(G)≤q, for q≥1.
claims.evidence: Extend a minimum dominating set to a q-set D. For current uncovered set U, the sets N[d]∩U for d∈D cover U, so their total cardinality is at least |U|. Thus some unselected vertex covers at least |U|/q newly uncovered vertices; already selected vertices cover none of U. Hence |U_i|≤(1−1/q)|U_{i−1}| and iteration gives the claimed bound. For q=1 the bound is zero and the argument is immediate.
claims.search_method: Recurrence proof plus exact check of r·q^q≤n·(q−1)^q on every simple graph on 1–6 vertices.

claims.claim: For arbitrary fixed c, greedy gives an exact polynomial-time triage: it solves the instance whenever r≤n/c or r>n(1-1/q)^q.
claims.evidence: On the natural domain q≥1, let S be the q distinct greedy vertices. Every residual vertex u lies outside S and has no edge to S, so adding one absent edge from a fixed s∈S to each u uses exactly r edits and makes S an exact q-dominating set. If r exceeds the displayed bound, Claim 1's contrapositive gives γ(G)>q, making (G,nil) correct. The comparison with the theoretical bound is r·q^q>n·(q−1)^q and has polynomial bit complexity. The source's standing convention requires the fixed radius function n/c to be polynomial-time computable. The q=0 input is separately trivial and does not lie in the displayed formula's domain.
claims.search_method: Constructive proof plus exact exhaustive tests for several rational c on every simple graph through order 6.

claims.claim: Sidestep(Dominating Set,dist_e,n/c) is in FP for every fixed c≤e.
claims.evidence: Within the target domain c>0, for q≥2, ln(1−1/q)≤−1/q gives (1−1/q)^q≤e^−1; q=1 is direct. Thus a nonviolating residual satisfies r≤n/e≤n/c and can be repaired by Claim 2, while a violating residual certifies nil for G. For q=0, the empty graph has the empty dominating set and every nonempty graph correctly yields nil. All operations, including the integer-power comparison, are polynomial-time.
claims.search_method: Analytic inequality and exhaustive exact-integer checks, including rational samples below e and all q≥1 through order 6.

claims.claim: For every c, all instances with q≥1 and n-q≤n/c have a direct polynomial-time YES output.
claims.evidence: Choose any q-set S and s∈S. Each vertex not dominated by S is outside S and nonadjacent to s. Adding su for every such vertex therefore uses distinct absent edges, at most n−q of them, and makes S dominate. The assumed inequality places the result within radius.
claims.search_method: Direct construction plus exhaustive exact-radius tests on every simple graph through order 6 for several rational c.

claims.claim: For every c, a computable sparse NO certificate is available when q+1 vertices have at most n/c incident edges in total.
claims.evidence: For an exhibited set T of q+1 vertices, delete the distinct edges having at least one endpoint in T. The edit count is its incident-edge count, and all vertices of T become isolated. Every dominating set must contain every isolated vertex, so the new graph has domination number at least q+1 and nil is correct. The certificate T and resulting graph are polynomially verifiable and constructible. A deterministic sufficient case is obtained by sorting degrees: the union of incident edges of the q+1 lowest-degree vertices is at most their degree sum.
claims.search_method: Certificate proof plus exhaustive deletion for every graph through order 6 and every possible nonempty T.

claims.claim: Domination number is one-Lipschitz per edge edit, with a constructive transfer.
claims.evidence: If S dominates H, let U be the vertices not dominated by S in G. Each u∈U is outside S and must have an H-only edge su to S. Different u give different edges, hence |U|≤|E(H)\E(G)|, and S∪U dominates G. Reversing G and H proves |γ(G)−γ(H)|≤|E(G)△E(H)|; a single edit changes γ by at most one. Computing U supplies the constructive transfer.
claims.search_method: Bidirectional proof plus exhaustive checking of every oriented one-edge edit and every dominating set on orders 0–4.

claims.claim: A radius-R sidestep solver decides every additive-gap instance whose YES case has γ(G)≤q-R and whose NO case has γ(G)>q+R.
claims.evidence: For any returned H at edit distance t≤R, Lipschitzness gives γ(H)≤γ(G)+t≤q in the YES case and γ(H)≥γ(G)−t>q in the NO case. By exact-size monotonicity, every H in the ball therefore has the corresponding output type, so the solver's set-versus-nil answer decides the promise.
claims.search_method: Lipschitz deduction plus exhaustive checking of all graph pairs, q, and integral radii through order 4.

claims.claim: Any FP solver at fixed c yields a polynomial-time additive-2⌊n/c⌋ approximation for Minimum Dominating Set.
claims.evidence: Let R=⌊n/c⌋ and run the solver for all q. For q0=min(n,γ(G)+R), every graph in the radius-R ball has domination number at most q0; if q0=n this is automatic. Hence the first YES threshold q* satisfies q*≤q0≤γ(G)+R. Transfer its exact q*-set from the returned H to G using Claim 6, adding at most R vertices. The resulting dominating set has size at most γ(G)+2R. There are only n+1 calls.
claims.search_method: Universal bound proof plus exhaustive adversarial checking over every possible returned graph and exact-q set through order 4.

claims.claim: On graphs of maximum degree Δ, the preceding algorithm is a (1+2(Δ+1)/c)-approximation.
claims.evidence: Every dominating vertex covers at most Δ+1 vertices, so n≤(Δ+1)γ(G). Since R=⌊n/c⌋≤n/c, the Claim 8 output is at most γ(G)+2n/c≤(1+2(Δ+1)/c)γ(G). The empty graph is handled separately with optimum and output both zero.
claims.search_method: Exact algebra plus exhaustive integer cross-multiplication on all graphs through order 6 for several rational c.

claims.claim: There is an exact approximation-preserving reduction from isolate-free Vertex Cover of maximum degree three to Dominating Set of maximum degree six.
claims.evidence: For each edge e=uv, retain uv and add x_e adjacent to u and v. A vertex cover dominates every x_e, and isolate-freeness ensures every unchosen original vertex has a chosen original neighbor. Conversely, N[x_e]⊆N[u] for either endpoint u, so replacing a selected x_e by an endpoint preserves domination and never increases cardinality. Once all selected vertices are original, domination of each x_e forces an endpoint of e into the set, yielding a vertex cover. Thus γ equals τ. Original degrees double to at most six and edge vertices have degree two.
claims.search_method: Bidirectional transformation proof plus exhaustive testing of 559 eligible input graphs through order 5 and every dominating-set conversion.

claims.claim: The universal target implies a PTAS family for cubic Minimum Vertex Cover.
claims.evidence: For any fixed ε>0, instantiate the universal target at c=14/ε. Claim 9 on the degree-six gadget gives ratio 1+14/c=1+ε. Claim 10 preserves the optimum and converts the returned dominating set into a no-larger vertex cover. Runtime is polynomial for each fixed ε, which is precisely the asserted PTAS family.
claims.search_method: Deductive composition of the additive approximation and exact gadget reduction.

claims.claim: Conditional on the standard APX-hardness theorem for cubic Vertex Cover, the universal target holds if and only if P=NP.
claims.evidence: Treating the stated hardness theorem as the premise, it supplies a fixed η>0 for which a polynomial (1+η)-approximation would force P=NP. Universal sidestepping instantiated at c=14/η supplies that approximation by Claim 11, proving the forward implication. If P=NP, Dominating Set witnesses can be recovered by polynomially many decision queries, enlarged to exactly q when necessary, and returned with H=G and zero edits for every c. This proves the reverse implication. No unconditional P≠NP assumption is smuggled into the claim.
claims.search_method: Logical verification of both directions under the explicitly stated APX-hardness premise.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for an unconditional FP algorithm for every fixed c>0. The draft rigorously supplies such an algorithm only for 0<c≤e. For arbitrary c it gives correct but incomplete triage and special cases, plus the conditional classification that the universal statement is equivalent to P=NP under the stated cubic-Vertex-Cover hardness theorem. That equivalence does not unconditionally prove or disprove the target, and no algorithm covering all c>e is supplied. The progress is nevertheless material. The final writeup expressly says that no unconditional all-c resolution is claimed and identifies the unresolved regime, so claimed_resolution=PARTIAL is accurate rather than overstated or understated.
